title: Why Agile Post-Quantum Cryptography Matters for Long-Lived Chip Designs
gist: A promotional overview of Synopsys' Agile PQC Public Key Accelerators, which combine hardware, firmware and software to support ML-KEM, ML-DSA and hash-based signatures alongside RSA/ECC, with firmware-updatable algorithms, side-channel countermeasures and an automotive functional-safety variant, aimed at long-lived products like vehicles and infrastructure.

insights.claim: Products expected to operate for many years, such as vehicles, industrial equipment, networking infrastructure and connected devices, need security that can evolve through their service lives, making quantum resilience a chip-development consideration today.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: PQC hardware IP demand will concentrate in long-lifecycle markets like automotive and infrastructure.

insights.claim: Digital trust depends on verifying that software updates come from authorized sources and communications originate from legitimate participants, so post-quantum key establishment and signatures are needed to protect these functions from future threats.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Secure boot and firmware-update authentication are the first PQC use cases to watch.

insights.claim: Synopsys' Agile PQC Public Key Accelerators support ML-KEM for shared-secret establishment, ML-DSA for digital signatures, and SLH-DSA, XMSS and LMS for hash-based signatures.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Broad standards coverage positions Synopsys IP for PQC migration designs.

insights.claim: The architecture supports established RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography alongside post-quantum algorithms, enabling staged migration while maintaining compatibility with existing infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Hybrid support lowers adoption friction for PQC transitions.
insights.locator: An encouraging aspect of the architecture

insights.claim: A firmware-driven control engine enables field updates to public-key algorithms, with firmware stored in RAM or ROM depending on configuration, though the practical benefit depends on the chosen architecture and secure update mechanisms.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Crypto agility hedges against algorithm changes over a product's life.

insights.claim: Processing resources, storage and firmware are configurable to balance performance, power and area, but specific performance and area results are configuration-dependent and the datasheet directs customers to Synopsys for benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: No public benchmarks given; competitive PPA versus rival PQC IP is unverified.

insights.claim: The offering includes a secure private-key interface for external key management and optional countermeasures against differential power analysis, timing analysis and fault injection.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Side-channel resistance is a key differentiator for hardware security IP.
insights.locator: The offering also addresses the protection

insights.claim: The automotive variant adds redundancy, fault detection, diagnostic reporting and safety monitoring with main and shadow processing paths, output comparison, memory protection and bus protection, and ships with safety and cybersecurity assessment materials.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Functional-safety-ready PQC IP targets automotive design wins as vehicle cybersecurity rules tighten.
